history.hpi: Woke abruptly around 0200 with severe air hunger and a sensation of drowning. Symptoms progressed rapidly over 20-30 minutes. Wife called 911 when he began coughing up pink, frothy sputum and could no longer speak in full sentences. Denies chest pain but reports significant anxiety and a feeling of impending doom. No recent illness, no leg swelling reported prior to tonight by patient (wife notes ankles have looked puffier the past week).
pastMedical: Coronary artery disease with prior stent
history.lastOralIntake: Dinner at 1900, ate salty takeout food
history.events: Sudden onset of severe dyspnea overnight, rapidly worsening, wife called 911 after pink frothy sputum appeared

scene.dispatch: 78-year-old male, difficulty breathing, conscious and breathing, residence
scene.location: Single-family home, second-floor bedroom, patient found sitting bolt upright on the edge of the bed
scene.safety: No hazards; narrow stairwell will complicate carrying equipment and patient down to the ambulance
scene.bystanders: Wife present, called 911 immediately, reports he has never had an episode like this before
visualCues: Patient sitting bolt upright, hands braced on knees, using accessory muscles
Visibly diaphoretic with pale, dusky skin
Pink, frothy sputum at the corners of the mouth
Audible wet crackling sounds without a stethoscope

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew finds a 78-year-old male in severe respiratory distress, sitting bolt upright, unable to speak more than 2-3 words at a time, with pink frothy sputum and diffuse crackles.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Severe accessory muscle use, unable to speak more than 2-3 words, RR 36
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses rapid and bounding, skin pale, cool, diaphoretic
otherFindings: Diffuse coarse crackles/rales audible bilaterally to the mid-lung fields
Pink, frothy sputum at the mouth
Extreme anxiety, sense of impending doom

transitions.condition: Crew recognizes flash pulmonary edema, applies CPAP promptly, and administers high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin given the severely elevated blood pressure.
Crew focuses on obtaining a full history or IV access before addressing the airway/oxygenation crisis, delaying CPAP and nitroglycerin administration.

phases.name: CPAP and nitro started
phases.description: Crew applies CPAP with coaching, screens for PDE5 inhibitor use, and administers high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin given the severely elevated blood pressure.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew recognizes flash pulmonary edema from the presentation (crackles, JVD, pink frothy sputum, severe hypertension) and immediately restores oxygenation/ventilation with CPAP while reducing preload/afterload with nitroglycerin.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, CPAP mask sealed and tolerated after coaching
clinicalPresentation.breathing: RR 28, accessory muscle use decreasing with positive pressure support
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong, skin still diaphoretic but color improving
otherFindings: CPAP mask sealed, patient coached through initial anxiety
No PDE5 inhibitor use reported by patient or wife
Crackles slightly improved with positive pressure

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply CPAP with coaching and reassurance; maintain continuous mask seal
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) should be administered for severe respiratory distress via BVM, continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) or bi-level positive airway pressure (BiPAP)
expectedActions.rationale: Restoring oxygenation and reducing work of breathing is the first priority in flash pulmonary edema.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Screen for PDE5 inhibitor use in past 48 hours before administering nitroglycerin
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: The use of nitrates should be avoided in any patient who has used a phosphodiesterase inhibitor within the past 48 hours. Examples are sildenafil, vardenafil and tadalafil, which are used for erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension.
expectedActions.rationale: Nitrates combined with PDE5 inhibitors can cause severe, refractory hypotension.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL, may repeat every 5 minutes while SBP remains greater than 100 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: SBP >= 160 mmHg or MAP greater than 120: Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL, can repeat every 5 minutes for SBP greater than 100 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Severe hypertension (SBP 224, MAP >120) warrants the higher nitroglycerin dose to rapidly reduce preload and afterload.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Place waveform capnography in line to monitor ventilatory status and response to CPAP
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Quantitative waveform capnography: Is indicated: For assessment and monitoring of ventilatory status in patients with significant respiratory distress, with or without airway adjuncts
expectedActions.rationale: Capnography helps confirm improving ventilation and detect early deterioration on CPAP.

transitions.condition: CPAP seal is maintained without interruption while nitroglycerin is repeated per protocol; patient's oxygenation and work of breathing steadily improve.
The CPAP mask seal is broken during movement or transport (e.g., to reposition or reassess the patient), causing rapid atelectasis and decompensation.

phases.name: Mask seal maintained continuously
phases.description: With continuous CPAP and repeated nitroglycerin, the patient's oxygenation, work of breathing, and blood pressure steadily improve during transport.
phases.triggerCondition: Continuous CPAP with an unbroken mask seal, combined with repeated nitroglycerin dosing per the blood pressure-based protocol, produces steady improvement in oxygenation and hemodynamics.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong and regular, skin warm and drying
otherFindings: Crackles markedly improved, now only faint bibasilar
Patient able to speak in full sentences through the CPAP mask breaks

expectedActions.shortAction: Maintain continuous CPAP seal through transport; do not remove until ED-ready to switch
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Once initiated and patient is tolerating mask, DO NOT discontinue CPAP/BiPAP until patient is on the emergency department stretcher and hospital CPAP/BiPAP is immediately available for patient to be switched over, or physician is at bedside and requesting CPAP/BiPAP be discontinued.
expectedActions.rationale: Breaking the seal causes rapid alveolar collapse and can reverse the clinical improvement.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess blood pressure before and after each nitroglycerin dose
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Nitroglycerin ... can repeat every 5 minutes for SBP greater than 100 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Repeat dosing is contingent on the patient maintaining an adequate systolic blood pressure.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

phases.name: CPAP seal broken during transport
phases.description: The CPAP mask seal is broken while moving the patient down the stairwell to the ambulance. Positive airway pressure is lost, and the patient rapidly decompensates.
phases.triggerCondition: The CPAP mask is removed or its seal broken during patient movement, causing abrupt loss of positive airway pressure and rapid atelectasis.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: RR 40, severe accessory muscle use returns abruptly
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses rapid, skin pale, cool, diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact but patient too dyspneic to cooperate with exam
otherFindings: Frothy sputum reappears at the mouth
Patient becoming increasingly obtunded from hypoxia

expectedActions.shortAction: Reseal and reapply CPAP mask immediately; do not delay for other interventions
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Breaking the mask seal causes a significant decrease in airway pressures and may lead to abrupt decompensation due to atelectasis and alveolar collapse.
expectedActions.rationale: Rapid recognition and correction of the broken seal is required to reverse the sudden decompensation.

phases.name: CPAP and nitro delayed
phases.description: The crew spends critical time on history-taking and IV attempts before addressing the airway and oxygenation crisis, allowing the patient to progress toward respiratory failure.
phases.triggerCondition: CPAP and nitroglycerin are delayed while the crew prioritizes history-gathering or IV access over immediate airway/oxygenation support.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Increasingly wet-sounding, gurgling with each breath
clinicalPresentation.breathing: RR 42, severe accessory muscle use, tiring
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses rapid and thready, skin ashen, cool, diaphoretic
otherFindings: Diminishing mental status from worsening hypoxia
Diffuse crackles throughout all lung fields
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: No longer able to speak, only gasping and gurgling

expectedActions.shortAction: Immediately apply CPAP and administer high-dose nitroglycerin now that impending respiratory failure is recognized
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Restoration of adequate oxygenation and ventilation should precede or be accomplished simultaneously with other medication therapies below
expectedActions.rationale: Delayed oxygenation support has allowed progression toward respiratory failure; immediate escalation is required to avoid needing intubation.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)
